@[nolint unusedHavesSuffices] -- Porting note: false positive
theorem strongDownwardInduction_eq {p : Finset α → Sort*}
    (H : ∀ t₁, (∀ {t₂ : Finset α}, #t₂ ≤ n → t₁ ⊂ t₂ → p t₂) → #t₁ ≤ n → p t₁)
    (s : Finset α) :
    strongDownwardInduction H s = H s fun {t} ht _ => strongDownwardInduction H t ht := by
  rw [strongDownwardInduction]

rag.name: Finset.case_strong_induction_on
rag.content:
@[elab_as_elim]
theorem case_strong_induction_on [DecidableEq α] {p : Finset α → Prop} (s : Finset α) (h₀ : p ∅)
    (h₁ : ∀ a s, a ∉ s → (∀ t ⊆ s, p t) → p (insert a s)) : p s :=
  Finset.strongInductionOn s fun s =>
    Finset.induction_on s (fun _ => h₀) fun a s n _ ih =>
      (h₁ a s n) fun t ss => ih _ (lt_of_le_of_lt ss (ssubset_insert n) : t < _)

informal_statement: For any type \( \alpha \), the Hilbert structure \( \text{Hilbert.KD}(\alpha) \) is a subset of \( \text{Hilbert.KDB}(\alpha) \). This means that \( \text{Hilbert.KD} \) is weaker than \( \text{Hilbert.KDB} \).
informal_proof:
To show that \( \text{Hilbert.KD}(\alpha) \leq_s \text{Hilbert.KDB}(\alpha) \), we need to demonstrate that every instance of \( \text{Hilbert.KD}(\alpha) \) is also an instance of \( \text{Hilbert.KDB}(\alpha) \).

We begin by noting that if we can show the inclusion of \( \text{Hilbert.KD}(\alpha) \) within \( \text{Hilbert.KDB}(\alpha) \), this would confirm that \( \text{Hilbert.KD} \) is indeed a weaker structure than \( \text{Hilbert.KDB} \).

Using the `aesop` tactic, we rely on automated reasoning to verify the subset relationship. This tactic systematically applies a series of simplification and logic rules to confirm that the inclusion holds. Upon successful application, it establishes that every element satisfying the conditions of \( \text{Hilbert.KD}(\alpha) \) also satisfies those of \( \text{Hilbert.KDB}(\alpha) \), thereby proving that \( \text{Hilbert.KD} \) is weaker than \( \text{Hilbert.KDB} \).
